denial.label: Pre-existing disease waiting period not completed

grounds: Osteoarthritis of knee was first diagnosed on 2026-03-21, AFTER the policy start date 2024-08-07; by definition it is not a Pre-Existing Disease, so the waiting period does not apply.
letter:
Subject: Appeal against Denial D03 – Pre‑Existing Disease Waiting Period – Claim ID be71eb6b-e150-4b83-b728-5eb1e5763b97  

Claim Details:  
- Claim ID: be71eb6b-e150-4b83-b728-5eb1e5763b97  
- Patient ID: 78be6008-8ddb-4c52-8b84-2f5f6b25aff6  
- Patient Name: Gopal Naidu  
- Date of Service: 2026-03-21  
- Policy: Suraksha Gold Family Floater Plan (Plan Code SGH‑GOLD)  
- Insurer: Suraksha General Health Insurance Ltd.  
- Total Claim Amount: INR 46,865.71  
- Diagnosis: Osteoarthritis of knee (onset 2026-03-21)  
- Procedure: Physical therapy  

Grounds for Appeal:  
The diagnosis of osteoarthritis of the knee was first made on 21 March 2026, which is after the policy start date of 7 August 2024. According to the policy definition, a condition first diagnosed on or after the policy start date is not a Pre‑Existing Disease and therefore the 24‑month waiting period does not apply [suraksha_gold_policy#5]. The waiting‑period clause itself confirms that it applies only to conditions meeting the definition of Pre‑Existing Disease [suraksha_gold_policy#10]. Consequently, the denial based on an alleged pre‑existing condition is inconsistent with the policy wording.  

Furthermore, under the insurer’s own denial standards, the burden of proof for any exclusion or waiting period lies with the insurer, who must provide documentary evidence that the condition existed before the policy start date. No such evidence has been supplied [claims_procedure_and_grievance#6].  

Clinical Necessity:  
Physical therapy is an essential component of the conservative management of knee osteoarthritis, which is required before consideration of surgical options such as total knee replacement. The clinical guideline states that total knee replacement is indicated only after at least three to six months of conservative treatment, underscoring the medical necessity of the prescribed physical therapy at this stage [knee_osteoarthritis#3]. The treating orthopaedic specialist will attach detailed clinical notes confirming the need for the therapy.  

Reference to Denial Standards and Appeal Rights:  
The insurer’s grievance procedure allows the insured or the provider to appeal a denial in writing within thirty days of the denial letter, identifying the claim, denial reason, relevant policy clauses, and supporting clinical evidence [claims_procedure_and_grievance#8]. This appeal is being submitted within the stipulated period. According to the same procedure, the insurer must acknowledge the appeal within three working days and render a decision within fifteen days, with payment of interest if the denial is overturned [claims_procedure_and_grievance#9].  

Specific Request:  
In view of the above, we respectfully request that the denial be withdrawn, the claim be re‑processed, and the amount of INR 46,865.71 be paid to the provider without further delay. If the decision is rendered after the statutory timeline, interest for the period of delay should be applied as per the grievance policy.  

Thank you for your prompt attention to this matter.  

Insurance Desk (on behalf of the treating provider)

citations.section: Suraksha Gold Family Floater Plan (Policy Wording) > 4. Waiting Periods > 4.2 Pre-Existing Disease Waiting Period
citations.quote:
### 4.2 Pre-Existing Disease Waiting Period
Expenses related to a Pre-Existing Disease (Clause 2.2) are covered after 24 months of continuous coverage from the first policy start date. This waiting period applies ONLY to conditions meeting the definition in Clause 2.2.

citations.section: Suraksha Gold Family Floater Plan (Policy Wording) > 2. Definitions > 2.2 Pre-Existing Disease (PED)
citations.quote:
### 2.2 Pre-Existing Disease (PED)
Pre-Existing Disease means any condition diagnosed by a physician, or for which medical advice or treatment was received, within 48 months PRIOR TO the first policy start date. citations.section: Claims Procedure, Denial Standards and Grievance Redressal > C3. Standards for Denial > C3.2 Burden of Proof for Exclusions and Waiting Periods
citations.quote:
### C3.2 Burden of Proof for Exclusions and Waiting Periods
The insurer bears the burden of proving that an exclusion or waiting period applies. For a Pre-Existing Disease denial, the insurer must show documentary evidence that the condition was diagnosed or treated before the policy start date.

citations.section: Claims Procedure, Denial Standards and Grievance Redressal > C4. Appeals and Grievances > C4.1 Right to Appeal
citations.quote:
## C4. Appeals and Grievances  
### C4.1 Right to Appeal
The insured, or the provider on the insured's behalf, may appeal a denial in writing within 30 days of the denial letter. The appeal should identify the claim, the denial reason, the policy clauses relied upon and the supporting clinical evidence.

citations.section: Knee Osteoarthritis — Conservative Care and Arthroplasty > Indications for Total Knee Replacement
citations.quote:
## Indications for Total Knee Replacement
Total knee replacement is indicated for severe pain and functional limitation despite at least 3–6 months of conservative treatment, with radiographic evidence of advanced joint-space narrowing (Kellgren–Lawrence grade 3–4).

citations.section: Claims Procedure, Denial Standards and Grievance Redressal > C4. Appeals and Grievances > C4.2 Timelines
citations.quote:
### C4.2 Timelines
The insurer's grievance cell must acknowledge an appeal within 3 working days and decide it within 15 days. If the denial is overturned, the claim must be paid with interest for the period of delay.
